summary: Chat kickoff starvation and elevated time-to-first-token following runtime queue rebalance
description:
Issue summary: Since the runtime queue-rebalance and scheduler tuning deployed 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC, several chat sessions for a high-volume dedicated customer show increased time-to-first-token (TTFB). Impact: Customer experiences 3-12s stalls before first token, occasional 504s for sessions that exceed request timeout. This is reproducible for short prompt+chat-init flows and appears more severe when KV cache is cold or when model pinning forces a model variant with different kernel selection.

Observed behavior: Conversations stall before streaming begins; first token latency spikes from baseline ~0.2-0.6s to 3-12s. Throughput for long-running token streaming is normal once streaming starts. Errors: sporadic 504s and 502s during peak.

Expected behavior: TTFB should remain at baseline (<1s) for dedicated capacity customer; no increase in 5xx rates after scheduler change.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovaDocs dedicated account in us-west region with model pinned to rw-medium-1.5
2) Start new chat session with a short priming prompt (30-80 tokens), enable streaming, low concurrency (1-2 sessions),
3) Observe initial token emission time via client-side timing and server traces
4) Repeat with KV cache cold and with KV cache warm (observe difference),
5) Compare before/after times relative to 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC rollout window

sample request-id: req_20260310_0f7c33 - first_token_latency=420ms - status=200 - model=rw-medium-1.5 - route=chat.completions.stream

investigation: 03-10 10:00 - Support (Aisha): Validated multiple request-ids from NovaDocs showing high first-token latencies and some 504s. Captured sample traces and forwarded to SRE.
03-10 11:15 - SRE (Diego): Correlated latency spikes with runtime queue-rebalance rollout at 2026-03-09 22:30 UTC. Noticed increased slot_acquire_wait in traces for affected requests.

03-10 12:20 - Eng (R&D runtime team): Observed that the new scheduler attempts to rebalance work across fewer worker threads to improve throughput, which increases time waiting for a worker to be assigned for short, low-token requests leading to head-of-line starvation for chat kickoff.

Hypothesis 1: Scheduler rebalance introduced increased worker assignment latency for short-lived chat priming requests, particularly when KV cache is cold and kernel selection path takes fallback, causing TTFB inflation.

Hypothesis 2: A change in queue affinity (hot-path batching) reduced priority for low-token streaming requests; combined with recent kernel selection logic this delays first-token emission while batch windows form.

Correlation: Issues are concentrated in dedicated customers on older quantized model variants where kernel fallback triggers extra cache warmup and the scheduler waits for a worker matching GPU/quantization profile.
Repro attempt: Re-running workload on staging with scheduler toggled to previous policy reproduces median TTFB at baseline; enabling rebalance policy reproduces 3-8s stalls.

Related artifacts: linked PR https://github.com/redwood-infer/runtime/pull/1846 contains the rebalance logic and scheduler config changes. Slack thread #support-ttfb: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C0123456

Potential risk if rollback: Rolling back scheduler rebalance may affect overall throughput/burst behavior; we need a targeted patch to prioritize short-lived chat priming requests (fast-path) while preserving rebalance benefits for long-running batches.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-10T10:05Z: Customer reports visible UX regressions; they are on a paid dedicated plan and rely on predictable startup latency for chat. Captured request IDs and forwarded to SRE.
Diego Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-10T11:22Z: Seeing slot_acquire_wait spikes in traces. Pinpointing scheduler rebalance window. Posting trace samples and initiating staging repro.

Liu Chen (Runtime Eng) - 2026-03-10T12:35Z: Confirmed reproduction in staging. Opening a small PR to add a short-path priority queue for chat-priming requests. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-infer/runtime/pull/1854
NovaDocs Support Rep (Jordan Lee) - 2026-03-10T13:10Z: Thanks — any ETA on fix? These stalls are causing support tickets from our users.
Diego Morales (SRE) - 2026-03-10T13:45Z: Temporary workaround applied to NovaDocs' dedicated pool: increased per-pool reserved workers for low-latency traffic. Monitoring for improvement.
Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-11T09:00Z: NovaDocs reports median TTFB reduced from ~4.6s to ~0.9s after reserved worker bump; still seeing occasional 3-5s outliers during peak.
resolution: Workaround: Increased reserved worker slots on NovaDocs dedicated pool and applied temporary scheduler override prioritizing short chat priming requests for the affected capacity. Temporary mitigation reduced median TTFB to ~0.9s but some outliers remain. Next steps: 1) Runtime team will merge PR #1854 to add a fast-path priority queue for chat priming (target rollout 2026-03-13 after QA), 2) Post-deploy, monitor TTFB and 5xx rates for 48 hours; 3) If PR does not fully resolve outliers, follow-up patch will refine worker affinity heuristics and KV cache warmup ordering. Linked fix PR: https://github.com/redwood-infer/runtime/pull/1854. Customer communicated and SLA credit under review.
followups: Merge PR #1854 and schedule canary rollout to 10% of dedicated pools 2026-03-13
Add TTFB synthetic checks to Redwood Console per-route dashboard and an alert when P50 > 1s or P95 > 3s
Postmortem to be created in Confluence after stabilization, owner: Diego Morales, due 2026-03-20
